reason: As written the falsifier does not discriminate; it is fixable. Defects: (1) Presentation confound. t*D-1 adds n new Boolean variables (t in F_{2^n} must be descended) and degree-4 generators (D is cubic in x1,x2 and t is linear). F4 max degree in arm B is therefore >=4 and rises with n for reasons unrelated to the singular locus. This is the presentation dependence the idea says it escapes. The control is a random quadratic system with no matched Rabinowitsch transform, so it cannot separate the presentation effect from a real saturation effect. (2) Ideals are identical on typical instances. With field equations the ideal is radical and zero-dimensional over F_2. A random target R has an F_2-point with x1=x2, x_i=0 or 2P=R only with probability about 2^(l-n), roughly 1e-2 at (n=13,l=6) and under 1e-4 for n>=21. In those cases I:D^inf = I, so arm B is arm A in a different presentation, and any degree gap measures presentation only. Where an instance has no solutions at all, both ideals are (1) and only the refutation degree is compared. (3) Wrong regime. l fixed at 4..6 with n=13..25 means 2l <= 12 << n, a strongly overdetermined system. The degree there is bounded by the l-dependent k+2 and by linear-algebra refutation. 'Flat in n' holds in both arms for trivial reasons. The Gaudry/Diem regime is l about n/m; measured D fits ceil(l/2)+4 at m=3 and l+4 at m=4, so n-trend at fixed l has no scaling content. (4) m=2 only (S_3). The open lever is m>=3 (S_4, S_5), where there are more diagonals (x_i=x_j for all pairs) and the closure cells (4,4),(4,5),(4,6) are unmeasured. (5) The final GB degree of the ideal of the saturated point set is vacuous: for a zero-dimensional radical ideal with s points the regularity is <=s, and s is O(1) at l about n/m, so ideal-level regularity cannot show a cap. The meaningful quantity is the degree needed to reach the (1)/point-set certificate, which is presentation-dependent. (6) Budget: 6 n x 3 l x 20 targets x 2 arms = 720 msolve runs plus controls. For arm B at n=25,l=6 there are 12+25=37 Boolean variables with degree 4-7 matrices (about 1e7 columns, estimated, not measured), which likely exceeds 20 CPU-min total. Counting F4 max deg from the msolve -v 2 table is a structural quantity (not wall time), which is acceptable, but F4 selection-strategy degree is only an upper bound on d_F, not the certified last fall degree. (7) Scaling to n=131: even a clean flat result at l<=6, n<=25 supports nothing at n=131 (l about 65), and degree flatness does not by itself give B*D^2<<N (cost of the degree-d solve is not addressed). Classify any outcome as toy evidence only, and as accounting unless the exponent in n changes.
fix: Redesign. (a) Regime: set l = ceil(n/2) for m=2 with n in {11,13,15,17,19,21}, giving 22-42 vars in arm A only. Add m=3 via `ic corpus --degree n --dimension l` S_4 instances at (n,l)=(9..13, 3..4); also run l = floor(n/2)-2 to see the overdetermined side. Use fewer than 6 n values if the budget requires. (b) Plant the singular locus so A and B differ as ideals. Per cell, take 10 planted targets R=2P with x(P) in V (forces an x1=x2 solution), 5 planted with a 2-torsion summand (x=0 in V), and 10 random targets (control: ideal(A)=ideal(B), verified by msolve normal-form check that t*D-1 reduces to a consistent system with the same solution count). (c) Presentation-matched controls on every arm: (i) the same system with extra n Boolean t-variables and equations t*D'-1 where D' is a random cubic in the same variable blocks (random_matched in ffd_semaev_core.py provides the null for A); (ii) A plus a redundant but equivalent t*D-1 with D replaced by an everywhere-unit (D=1) to price the variable/degree overhead; (iii) a random quadratic Boolean system of identical shape, with the same Rabinowitsch transform applied. The test statistic is the double difference [deg(B)-deg(A)]_Semaev - [deg(B')-deg(A')]_control, not deg(B)-deg(A). (d) Measure both msolve -g 2 -v 2 max F4 round degree and, for arm A, the certified d_F via hky_last_fall_degree (cell --n N --draws K --cmax C) and ffd_semaev_core.fall_profile. For B use per-degree Macaulay rank profile or the first degree where the (1)/point-set certificate appears, not the final GB degree. Report solution counts before/after and the number of solutions removed by D. (e) Decision rule: TRUE only if the double difference is <=-1 on >=80% of planted AND random instances at the largest n of each l=ceil(n/2) series and the sign is stable across >=4 n values; if the effect appears only on planted instances, record it as singular-locus bookkeeping (accounting), not a d_F cap. FALSE if the double difference is >=0 or if (A) and (B) have equal ideals on all random instances (expected, so a null on random targets is vacuous and must not be reported as refutation). (f) Report class: toy evidence, accounting unless the n-exponent of deg changes. Scaling to n=131 is by extrapolation of deg vs (n, l=n/2) only; state that no claim about B*D^2<<N follows from a flat degree. (g) Budget: cap each msolve at 60 s, record timeouts as censored data, run arm A for all cells first and arm B only where A finished in <5 s. Estimated 10-18 CPU-min with this pruning.
